verdicts.rewritten_summary: Korea Times (22 July 2024): the Seoul appellate court dismissed the state's appeal and finalised a 300,000 won damages award (against a 3 million won claim), ruling that police advice to a person transitioning from male to female - who had obtained court approval for a family-register gender change in 2020 - to avoid women's public restrooms infringed personal rights; the appellate court held that comfortable restroom use is a fundamental and universal human right. The article also reports a 2021 NHRCK survey of 591 transgender respondents (41% used a restroom of a different gender, 39% avoided food and drink, 36% forwent restroom use) and a 2021 Daegu District Court (Pohang branch) award of 7 million won against a beauty academy that prohibited a transgender student from using its restroom. This is the national framework this province is scored against; no KOR/Gangwon-specific incident appears.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Yonhap wire (8 May 2024): a regional court in Yeongdong approved changing the registered sex from male to female for five transgender applicants without sex-reassignment surgery, holding that it is against the law to determine gender change based on surgery and that court guidelines requiring surgery are now only reference, not criteria; the court said every human being has the right to form their character and live a life according to their gender identity. The ruling removed the surgical prerequisite for registered-sex change and is the framework this province is scored against; the wire contains no KOR/Gangwon-specific content.
